clue.text: One of two standard Russian tools

definitions.text: One of two standard Russian tools

parts.words: One of two standard Russian tools
parts.note: the Soviet standard, or flag, showed two crossed implements, a hammer and a curved reaping blade; this is the second

explanation.definitionFit: The curved harvesting blade crossed with a hammer was the emblem on the Soviet flag.

clue.text: A number in a quiet setting provide music

indicators.note: setting, as a jewel's mount, surrounds what is put in it

parts.note: serene means calm and quiet
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A song placed in a peaceful scene makes music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' looks like a song but is D, 500 in Roman numerals; A and D sit inside SERENE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing or play to a loved one, traditionally at night under a window, is to make music for them.

clue.text: Main event

parts.note: main is an old word for a match between gamecocks, so a main event is a bird fight

explanation.definitionFit: A main was historically a series of matches in which roosters were set to battle.

clue.text: Rounds of drinks?

parts.note: rounds are circuits of a track, and an animal drinks by lapping; not bar rounds at all

explanation.definitionFit: Circuits of a race track are rounds, and a cat drinks by lapping, so the word covers both.

clue.text: Cat's coat poorly clipped

indicators.note: done poorly, the letters of the two words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A cat's fur has been badly trimmed by its groomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clipped' looks like part of the grooming picture, but it is the definition, the musical term for short detached notes; 'poorly' rearranges CATSCOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a staccato passage is played with each note short and detached, as if cut off.

clue.text: Syrup well described by Dormouse

parts.note: at the Mad Tea-Party in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, the Dormouse tells of three sisters living at the bottom of a well of syrup

explanation.definitionFit: Golden syrup or molasses is the dark sweet syrup of the Dormouse's well in Lewis Carroll's story.

clue.text: Swindles, theft and intrigue

parts.note: cons are swindles or confidence tricks
piracy is theft, at sea or of copyright material

explanation.surface: A list of crimes: frauds, stealing and plotting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' links the charade to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret plot by several people is an intrigue or scheme.

clue.text: Excuse for the absent-minded

parts.note: not a forgetful person's excuse, but a plea that one was absent, somewhere else, when a crime happened

explanation.definitionFit: A defence claiming the accused was elsewhere when the crime took place is an excuse for one who was away.

clue.text: Back in ballet, Ted offered Swan Lake role

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ted has been given a part back in a ballet production.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters ETTEDO run across 'ballet, Ted offered'; 'Back' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: The swan princess heroine of Tchaikovsky's ballet is its leading female role.

clue.text: Great Britain and N. ireland lifted suspension for Gulf state

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the letters are turned upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland is abbreviated UK
a wait is a pause or suspension of activity

explanation.surface: Britain lifts its suspension of relations with a Middle Eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'lifted' means read upwards, so the abbreviation is turned round before the pause is added.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil-rich emirate at the head of the Persian Gulf is a Gulf state.

clue.text: Recovery results in delight round the city

indicators.note: the word for delight goes round, enclosing the letters for the city

parts.note: rapture is intense delight
EC is the postal code of the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: A patient's return to health brings joy throughout the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the city' is the City of London, whose postcode area gives the inserted pair; 'results in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking something back after losing it is getting it back, a regaining or retrieval.

clue.text: One is creating a din

indicators.note: creating suggests the letters are worked up into something new

explanation.surface: Someone is making a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creating' rearranges ONEIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A din is a loud unpleasant sound, a racket.

clue.text: The earth's core, of nickel and iron

parts.note: Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, from Latin ferrum

explanation.surface: A science lesson describing what lies at the centre of our planet.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is nearly literal: geologists named the planet's core material from the two element symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists coined the term for the hypothesised metallic material of the planet's centre, made mostly of those two metals.

clue.text: A striking end to the game

definitions.text: A striking end to the game

parts.words: A striking end to the game
parts.note: read as a lit stick's tip, or as the final winning point in tennis that can end a contest

explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the point that, if won, wins the whole contest is a decisive, often dramatic close.

clue.text: Creatures that ruin the marrows

indicators.note: to ruin is to wreck, so the letters are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Pests that spoil a gardener's vegetable marrows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruin' rearranges THEMARROWS; a marrow is a large British vegetable like an overgrown courgette.
explanation.definitionFit: Burrowing soil invertebrates are creatures, a broad term for animals.

clue.text: Chow-wagon?

parts.note: a chow is a breed of dog, so a wagon for chows would be a cart for dogs; really a light two-wheeled carriage

explanation.definitionFit: A light two-wheeled horse carriage, originally with a box under the seat to carry sporting hounds.

clue.text: Unrefined and extravagantly hearty

indicators.note: extravagantly suggests the letters are thrown about wildly

explanation.surface: A coarse person who is over-the-top in their heartiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extravagantly' rearranges HEARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse, down-to-earth humour or manners are crude and unpolished.

clue.text: It suffers periodic reversals in time

definitions.text: It suffers periodic reversals in time

parts.words: It suffers periodic reversals in time
parts.note: a sand timer is turned upside down each time its sand runs out

explanation.definitionFit: A sand timer measures time and is inverted at regular intervals to restart.

clue.text: Rose, as the century drew to a close

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for century, from the Roman numeral for 100
ended means finished or drew to a close

explanation.surface: Someone stood up as the hundred years came to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a flower or name but is the verb; C is century.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose as a past tense means went up or climbed.

clue.text: Says they may follow United

definitions.meaning: the word after United in the name of the USA, or the Arab Emirates' neighbour phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition fills a blank: United ___ of America.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare is to put into words; the word also completes the country name after United.

clue.text: Spider and fly

definitions.meaning: a creature that weaves a web
an angler's artificial lure that revolves in the water

explanation.definitionFit: A web-weaving creature and a revolving fishing lure share one name.

clue.text: A trip with passengers, we hear, makes profits

indicators.note: we hear signals that the phrase is to be said out loud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a voyage carrying passengers is a cruise, so this gives a cruise

explanation.surface: A tour operator's passenger trips are making money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a cruise' and the answer sound identical when spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest that builds up or accumulates over time is gained, piling up as profit.

clue.text: Received a hero's treatment when landed

indicators.note: giving the letters treatment works them over into a new order

explanation.surface: A returning hero is fêted on stepping off the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges AHEROS; 'Received' and 'when' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone landed is on dry ground, no longer at sea.

clue.text: Pub arranged to have meals in every bar

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the word are put in another order

parts.note: to eat is to have meals

explanation.surface: A pub has set up food service at every counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub counter but is a musical measure; 'arranged' turns PUB into UPB, then EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The unaccented beat before a downbeat occurs once in every musical measure.

clue.text: Dramatist in predicament is unusually wary

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for predicament

parts.note: a plight is a predicament or dire situation

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of wary appear in a strange order

explanation.surface: A stage writer in a tight spot is uncommonly cautious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges the four letters of 'wary' to AYWR, and 'in' places them within the word for a tight spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of plays for the stage is a dramatist.

clue.text: Where two sides get together to some degree

definitions.text: Where two sides get together to some degree

parts.words: Where two sides get together to some degree
parts.note: two lines meeting at a corner, measured in degrees, read as rival parties partly agreeing

explanation.definitionFit: The figure formed where two lines meet is measured in degrees.

clue.text: Monster note in Scandinavian currency

indicators.note: in places the note's letter within the currency word

parts.note: the ore is a small coin of Sweden, Norway and Denmark
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A frightening banknote in a Nordic country's money.
explanation.walkthrough: G goes inside ORE, the hundredth part of a Scandinavian krona or krone.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating giant of folklore is a monster.

clue.text: It takes me only a jiffy to write a note

parts.note: mo, short for moment, means a jiffy

explanation.surface: Someone boasts they can dash off a letter in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is informal British for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A short written message, as in an office, is a note.

clue.text: Anxious to agree somehow

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters reach the result by some unknown rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is nervous about consenting in any way they can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges AGREE; 'Anxious' here means keen rather than worried.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious to do something can mean keen or impatient to do it.

clue.text: From USA, minder comes for a small charge

indicators.note: made from the letters of these words, rearranged

explanation.surface: An American childminder arrives, working for a low fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' rearranges USAMINDER. 'small charge' looks like a modest fee, but the charge is a child in someone's care.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after young children has a little one in her care.

clue.text: Wealth of much-loved person

definitions.meaning: riches or a hoard of valuables, a noun
a darling or someone highly prized

explanation.walkthrough: 'of' joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoard of riches is wealth, and a person much valued is called by the same word.

clue.text: Stimulated, the staff is about to exercise

indicators.note: is about tells us the staff goes round the other word

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
to use a power or right is to exercise it

explanation.surface: Someone energised: the staff are about to work out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but is a stick, which 'is about' wraps round the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred up or awakened, as by an exciting stimulus.
